judge_assessment.explanation: The arithmetic the judge cites is exact -- I re-derived all of it from the worksheet: x=5 (3x+7=22), x=5 with AB=13, x=12 with m<ABC=58, x=9, x=35 with m<AEC=115, x=8, x=22 with 98 and 82, and the synthesis x=8 with m<ABC=52 (check: m<ABD=26, twice 26 = 52). The judge's page criticism is real but overstated. It scored visual_and_print_quality 3 for 'inefficient use of seven worksheet pages', yet scripts/page_budget.py computed this sheet's own allowance and the gate log records 'Page budget (ws, letter): 10 problems, 139.5cm of content / ideal 6 page(s) - accepted range 4-8', with the compile step reporting '7 page(s), within the 8-page budget'. The sheet is one page above its computed ideal and inside the accepted band, on a system whose budget deliberately buys work space rather than capping it. The overrun also has a diagnosed cause the judge did not name: the budget note states '3 problem block(s) are taller than half a page, so only one fits per page and the rest of each page is stranded' -- problems 5, 8 and 9 -- and prescribes the fix (a shorter block, not a bigger workspace). Separately, the judge missed a coverage gap: problems 2, 3, 6 and 8 each open by asking the student to NAME the postulate, definition or theorem, and none of those four ids carries a manual entry, while the written parts of problems 1, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10 all do.

strengths_to_preserve: The interleaving is genuine rather than cosmetic: after the warm-up the sheet alternates algebraic proof, segment argument, angle argument and full two-column proof (facets algebraic-proof / segment-argument / angle-argument / two-column-proof in verify.json), so the student has to choose a method rather than repeat the previous skeleton -- problem 7 even plants a classmate's wrong FIRST MOVE (4x-5 = 2x+7) so the choice itself is the error being analysed.

Problem 10 is a well-formed synthesis: part (a) asks for a sentence-level argument that must END at the equation 7x-4 = 2(2x+10), so the student cannot start from the algebra, and part (b) then solves the equation they justified.
Problem 5 asks for AN = (1/4)AB, which forces the definition of midpoint to be applied twice and then substituted -- a two-application proof that a single midpoint problem cannot elicit.

The directions state the discipline the sheet is testing before problem 1: 'A diagram can suggest a relationship, but only the givens and what follows from them may be used as reasons', which is exactly the rule problems 2, 5, 8 and 9's figures could otherwise undermine.

root_causes.description: A 'name the postulate/definition/theorem' request that shares a problem with a numeric part is left uncovered: the numeric entries satisfy per-id coverage, so the naming answer is neither machine-checked (no type can check a name) nor declared manual. The sheet applies its own convention inconsistently -- six problems flag their written half, four do not.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 2: 'Name the postulate that lets you combine the three givens into one equation. Then find x, and use it to find AB.' -- verify.json id 2 holds only a solve (x=5) and an eval (AB=13).
worksheet.tex problem 3: 'State the definition that makes the two expressions equal ...' -- id 3 holds only solve (x=12) and eval (58).
worksheet.tex problem 6: 'Name the postulate that tells you what the two measures add to ...' -- id 6 holds only solve (x=35) and eval (115).
worksheet.tex problem 8: 'Name the theorem that relates
By contrast ids 1, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10 each carry a manual entry, and answer_key.pdf prints 'Manual-review item' under exactly those six problems and under none of 2, 3, 6, 8.
The judge counted 8 manual items reviewed against the 6 declared in verify.json, i.e. an independent reader also saw more open responses than the file declares.

root_causes.description: Three problem blocks exceed half a page because a tall TikZ figure and a full-height workspace are stacked vertically, so each strands the remainder of its page. The page budget charges for the stranding and still passes, so nothing in the chain pushes the author toward the shorter block the budget note itself recommends.
evidence: gate_log.txt step 13: 'Page budget (ws, letter): 10 problems, 139.5cm of content / ideal 6 page(s) - accepted range 4-8' and 'NOTE: 3 problem block(s) are taller than half a page ... the fix is a SHORTER BLOCK -- a smaller figure, or workspace beside the figure instead of under it -- not a larger workspace_cm'.
worksheet.pdf page 5 carries problem 8 alone (transversal figure plus \problem[8cm]); pages 6 and 7 each carry one problem (the 5-row proof tables of problems 9 and 10's synthesis).
Page 1 carries the title block, the four-item directions list and problem 1 alone, whose \problem[7cm] workspace is the largest on the sheet for the easiest item (a two-step equation).

improvements.title: Give the 'name the postulate/definition/theorem' request in problems 2, 3, 6 and 8 its own manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the coverage rule so a check is required per requested response, not per problem id, and enforce it in the gate chain: count the imperative request cues inside each \problem body ('Name the', 'State the', 'Say which', lettered parts) and fail when an id's request count exceeds its verify-entry count. On this sheet that forces four manual entries whose desc names the expected authority (Segment Addition Postulate; definition of an angle bisector; Linear Pair Postulate; same-side interior angles theorem), and the answer key would then carry the matching grading note as it already does for problems 1, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a problem body reading 'Name the postulate that lets you combine the givens. Then find x.' with a verify id carrying only a solve entry -- the checker must exit non-zero naming the uncovered request, and must pass once a manual entry is added to that id. curr-305 builds green today (layout-ws PASS, verify-ws MANUAL from the other six ids), so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: On a sheet whose stated purpose is 'constructing coherent multi-step arguments from stated givens', the named authority stops being the one requested answer nobody checks, and the manual count reported to the teacher (6) matches what the sheet actually asks a human to grade (10).
improvements.risk: Cue counting can over-fire on narrative prose, so it must be scoped to \problem bodies and allow an explicit author override; back-filling existing verify.json files across the corpus will surface many similar ids at once.

improvements.title: Shorten the three over-half-page blocks so the sheet lands on its computed ideal page count
improvements.proposed_change: Act on the advice scripts/page_budget.py already prints instead of only recording it: when a problem block exceeds half a page, SKILL.md should direct the author to shorten the block -- reduce the TikZ scale, or place the workspace beside a narrow figure rather than under it -- and page_budget.py should name the offending problem ids in its NOTE (it currently reports only a count) so the author knows which three to fix. For this sheet that means shrinking the transversal figure in problem 8 and the two triangle/segment figures above the proof tables in problems 5 and 9, and trimming problem 1's 7 cm workspace, which is the largest on the sheet for its easiest item.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_page_budget.py, build a verify.json whose blocks exceed half a page and assert the emitted NOTE lists the specific problem ids responsible; today the note reports only '3 problem block(s) are taller than half a page', so the assertion fails before the change and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Recovers roughly one page of the seven and removes the 'unusually page-spread' impression that cost this case its only lost point, without reducing any student's work space -- the stranded space is recovered from layout, not from the workspace.
improvements.risk: Shrinking figures trades page count against figure legibility; any reduction must stay inside the layout gate's minimum figure and workspace thresholds, and the answer-line and overprint gates should be re-run on the rebuilt sheet.

case_summary: A comprehensive interleaved proof set that is mathematically clean: all ten problems re-solve to the published values (x = 5, 5, 12, 9, 35, 8, 22, 8 with AB=13, m<ABC=58, m<AEC=115, m<p=98, m<q=82, m<ABC=52), the two blank proof tables are correctly declared manual, and the synthesis problem is well constructed because part (a) must terminate at the equation part (b) solves. Two findings beyond the judge. First, the four problems that ask the student to NAME the postulate, definition or theorem (2, 3, 6, 8) carry no manual entry, while the six problems whose written parts are flagged show the sheet's own convention -- and the judge's own count of 8 manual items against the file's 6 is a symptom of the same gap. Second, on the seven-page criticism I only partly agree: the computed budget for this content is 'ideal 6, accepted 4-8', the sheet came in at 7, and the gate log already names the cause (three blocks taller than half a page) and the remedy (shorter blocks, not bigger workspaces).
